project_metadata.job_description:
Need Designer for Magazine Layout & Prepress Formatting


We are looking for someone with Magazine layout and type setting experience. We need to launch our magazine in 10 days and need it ready for physical print as well as (PDF to Digital Flip Book). The magazine will have 100 pages or less.

We will supply you the articles (Word Documents) and you need to handle the creation of the template, type setting, and layout. No graphic design from scratch is needed. 
Any advertisement pages will come to you already designed as PSD files.

***The person we hire will help us with the structure and arrangement of the magazine. 

-You will arrange provided articles (text and images) into a cohesive magazine layout.
-No original design work required; all design elements will be supplied.
-Deliver two outputs: a PDF suitable for digital flipbook use, and a print-ready version at 300 dpi.
-Magazine length: approximately 100 pages.

*The budget is $100 USD. Any bids higher, will be discarded. 

We would like to hire this person for ongoing monthly relationship.

Hi WB,

Okay, they're not exactly typos but punctuation inconsistencies like en dash "–" in place of em dash "—" or using them both with spaces "word — word" and without spaces "word—word" — the style has to be consistent. I'd keep it "word — word" throughout. For eg., "Charlie Kirk – The Best and Greatest of Us" title on the web uses en dash "–" and not em dash "—", so it has to be "Charlie Kirk — The Best and Greatest of Us". Also, I'd add period at the end of complete sentences even in blurbs and points, which I find missing at many places, for e.g., "Family: Married to Jeanette Dousdebes Rubio since 1998; the couple has four children" — I hope it makes sense.

Points corresponding your feedback:

1\. The inconsistent empty spaces at the end of most articles is not only about the layout, font, images — it's more to do with the length of the content, because the articles were created for web and not for magazine editorial. The traditional or ideal way of addressing this issue is to add more text — because in magazine or newspaper editorial, word count is very crucial. The layout is always done using dummy text "Lorem Ipsum" based on the approximate word count per page that you get from the editorial team; and then you balance it with images and blurbs. After the layout is completed in terms of the pagination requirements, the editorial team works based on the word count of the dummy text. However, in case of pre-written articles, the author or the editorial team would cut short or add more text to match the word count. So, in our situation, I did what best could be done — to balance with images and even with text kerning. But, in order to achieve like "Confirmed Alien Existence Can’t Cast Doubt on Christianity' article" — we need to add more text, and/or images where possible. For example, for "Made in the USA: The Return of Domestic Manufacturing", we can add a big image on page 24 to cover up page 25 as much as possible — but for exact consistency, adding more text to match the word count is the only way ahead. Based on this criteria, you can send me more images wherever you think we can add in order to fill up the white space toward the end, as much as possible.

2\. This is an optimized version, besides the ads are not replaced yet with the PSD versions you sent — they'll all be fixed in the next version.

3\. If you're referring to the body font, then it's the same font that you've used on your website. However, please see attached 3 alternative options — I'd go with **Inter** font.

4\. I've sent you a spread version to give you a better idea of the layout. For Flip Book, we'll have to upload the pages version. The page count should be even, i.e., divisible by 2. Sure, I'll test it on <http://Hezine.com> once we're though with this.

5\. If you're happy with the pagination order of the articles, then I can go ahead with the Table of Contents.

We need 1 ad now to fill up the empty page 99. But you can send me 2-3 more ads, just in case if needed.

Many thanks!

BK

Hi WB,

Thanks for the feedback and the ads.

My responses:

1\. Are you sure about Garamond for body text? It's a serif font style that works best for novels, memoirs, journals, and artsy-style large-format books/magazines like interior design and the likes. For modern magazine layouts, a semi-condensed san serif font is highly recommended, especially when paired with a serif font for heading. Trust me, **INTER** font is much better in terms of thickness, legibility, spacing, and modern appeal.

2\. Yes, for next issue, I'll do the layouts with dummy text and we'll work as per exact word count in tandem with other elements.

3\. Thanks for the ads.

4\. Okay, I'll work on the Table of Contents today.

5\. Sure, I'll let you know once I've tested the Flip Book.

Many thanks,

BK

messages.text:
And this is the review for you:

BhaveshKumar did an exceptional job on our magazine layout and prepress formatting project. He handled every aspect of the assignment with professionalism, precision, and great attention to detail.

He took our articles, images, advertisements, and other supplied materials and organized them into a cohesive, polished, and visually consistent magazine. The typography, spacing, page structure, article flow, and overall presentation were all handled extremely well. He also demonstrated a strong understanding of both magazine production and prepress requirements, delivering files that were properly prepared for physical printing as well as digital flipbook distribution.

BhaveshKumar was dependable, responsive, patient with revisions, and committed to producing the best possible final product. He worked efficiently under a demanding deadline without sacrificing quality and consistently communicated clearly throughout the project.

He exceeded our expectations in every area. I highly recommend BhaveshKumar to anyone looking for a skilled, reliable, and detail-oriented magazine layout and prepress professional. We would absolutely hire him again!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Just one humble request... If you truly believe this, then please put the words into action by adding a bonus — whatever you think is fair, no compulsion — I'd greatly appreciate whatever helps in overcoming my misery of doing such hard labor of nearly 50 hours for literally nothing!!! If it was some other client, I'd have easily charged +$1000.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: And after all the deductions — I'd finally get about $84 in my account — Do you think it's really worth it?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you as well!

And I do believe that and I also want to help you. And I will send you a bonus so you get the full $100 tomorrow.

What we are after as a partner that we can grow together with. But we are a start up and none of the ads in the magazine are paid ads, so we have zero income until the magazine can get noticed and grow. With that said, if you feel that the project compensation is too low, I completely understand. But please send me the created template so we can try to do the next issue ourselves then.

I appreciated!

Whilly

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Could you please make it another $100 as bonus? — of course that isn't too much I'm asking — you would easily spend that over lunch or dinner at a restaurant. Don't I deserve it for putting my heart and soul into your product???

Of course I want to work as a partner and develop the relationship. But does that mean you'd only pay $100 per issue, every month? — even when you start selling the ads??? There has to be some mutually beneficial roadmap to this relationship. Right now it seems all one-sided, and then you even want the source files — c'mon! It sounds like exploiting someone's nice and humble nature. Would you like to be treated that way?

I've started 3 magazines myself so I know how the business works. But you do start a business with some budget — and your budget just can't be so low when producing a high-quality niche product.

I definitely want to do the next issue — of course, for Stallone!!! But we sincerely need to figure out how we're going to make this relationship work in the long run.

Think over it buddy. I'm not expecting immediate answers. Take your time.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
It may feel or seem that way, but the truth is more simple. This magazine is just an idea with exactly what you mentioned.. 'no budget'. So there is no greed or anything bad, just really don't have any funds for this start up. Even $20 is a lot of money right now. But if and when ads start to sell, of course that $100 would be increased to $250, $500, etc. But were starting from zero.

The main thing is that both sides have to be happy, otherwise its not worth it. So please send me the template, I already released the funds, and then I will leave you the feedback / review and we can continue to the conversation.

Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Okay, makes sense, if you're really serious about this partnership. Could you please make it $50 at least? That's how much someone would normally spend at Starbucks at once. Please! That would make me happy for now bro.

And I'm doing the next issue for sure — for Stallone!!! We could possibly discuss a bundle deal that includes content creation, website management, social media posts, etc. What say?

I wish you all the success with this new venture. I hope you make a lot of money, and then compensate me accordingly. By the way, many clients have found my association quite lucky for their businesses.

Good luck!

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Of course Im serious. Please send over the template we we can conclude this project and continue from there. Thanks
